---
title: "Extraction pipeline"
subtitle: "Fields first, then documents --- and the documents may only add"
---

Extraction happens in two steps with a hard boundary between them.

**Step 1 --- relational.** Typed endpoints map into the document shape. Every
value is authoritative and every gap is explicit (`None`).

**Step 2 --- model.** A cheap model screens the harvested documents, a strong one
reads the survivors, and the result is merged *additively*: a field that already
holds a value is never written, whatever the model says.

The boundary is the design. If step 2 returned a rewritten document, finding out
what it changed would mean diffing and trusting the diff. Returning only
*additions* makes "nothing existing was changed" true by construction --- no code
path in `merge.py` writes to a field that holds a value.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph s1["Step 1 · Relational"]
    direction LR
    A["session.py<br/>typed pulls"] --> B["activities.py<br/>per-type records"]
    B --> C["document.py<br/>one doc per course"]
  end
  subgraph s2["Step 2 · Model"]
    direction LR
    D["documents.py<br/>corpus → content blocks"] --> E["screen.py<br/>Pass 1 · relevant?"]
    E -->|"relevant only"| F["extract.py<br/>Pass 2 · proposal"]
    F --> G["merge.py<br/>additive merge"]
  end
  C --> H[("moodle.sqlite")]
  H -->|"record as input"| F
  G --> H

  classDef llm fill:#eef3fb,stroke:#7fa8d8
  class E,F llm
```

Note the loop: the step-1 document is *input* to pass 2. The model is shown what
is already known so it can be told to propose only where it sees `null`.

# Step 1 --- relational

`CourseDocumentBuilder.build_all()` makes one call per *source*, not per course
--- the `*_by_courses` endpoints accept a course list --- then slices the results
per course.

```python
quizzes     = session.quizzes(ids, include_empty=False)
assignments = session.assignments(ids, include_empty=False)
workshops   = session.workshops(ids, include_empty=False)
lessons     = session.lessons(ids, include_empty=False)
quiz_state   = {q["instance"]: q for q in session.quiz_status(quizzes)}
assign_state = {a["instance"]: a for a in session.assignment_status(assignments)}
```

Each type then goes through its own mapper (`_quiz`, `_assignment`, `_workshop`,
`_lesson`) which joins the activity record with the user's state for it.

Two conventions hold across the whole document:

**Dates are stored twice.** `due_at` (unix) is the source of truth and the only
field that may be sorted or compared. `due_date` / `due_time` are pre-rendered
in `Europe/Zurich` so consumers never format on the fly. Every type is
normalised to `due_at` regardless of what Moodle calls it --- a workshop's
submission end, a lesson's deadline, a quiz's close time.

**`None` and `[]` differ.** `[]` means fetched and genuinely none; `None` means
never attempted. This is what makes the gaps in the document legible rather than
ambiguous, and `None` is precisely what step 2 is allowed to fill.

Derived fields are kept minimal and explicit:

```python
# A quiz with no maximum grade cannot count toward the module mark.
"is_graded": None if grade_max is None else grade_max > 0,
```

The fields step 1 *cannot* answer, which is the entire reason step 2 exists:

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `general.credits` | No Moodle endpoint exposes ECTS |
| `grading[]` | Weights live in syllabus PDFs |
| `mandatory_onsite[]` | Attendance rules live in prose |
| `grade_achieved` (non-quiz) | Needs the gradebook; not pulled |

# Step 2 --- the model passes

## Preparing documents

`extraction/documents.py` turns each corpus file into Messages-API content
blocks, or records why it cannot. Three readable shapes:

| Medium | Source | Block type |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | HTML stripped to visible words, plus `.md`/`.txt`/`.csv`/`.ipynb`/code | `text` |
| `image` | PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, base64 | `image` |
| `pdf` | The PDF's own bytes | `document` |

A PDF takes the **text** route when it has a real text layer, and the far more
expensive **pdf** route only when extraction yields under
`MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE` (100) characters per page --- the signal of a scan. Scanned
PDFs are capped at `MAX_SCANNED_PAGES` (20), since each page costs image tokens.

Unreadable files are returned *with a reason*, never dropped:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inert format (.css)` | Cannot carry course information → verdict `False`, free |
| `needs conversion (.docx)` | Could carry it, cannot be opened yet → verdict `None` |
| `unhandled format (…)` | Unknown extension → verdict `None` |
| `no extractable text` | Opened, empty |

A format nothing can parse is a **gap in coverage**, and a gap no one can see is
worse than one that is recorded. This is why `relevant` is tri-state.

## Pass 1 --- screening

One cheap call per document answering one question: does this say anything about
how the course is *run*?

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["corpus<br/>243 documents"] --> B{"readable?"}
  B -->|"inert format"| C["False<br/><i>free, no call</i>"]
  B -->|"cannot parse"| D["None<br/><i>free, no call</i>"]
  B -->|yes| E["claude-haiku-4-5<br/>8 workers"]
  E --> F["True · 32"]
  E --> G["False · 209"]
  F --> H["pass 2 reads these"]
```

- **Model** `claude-haiku-4-5`, `SCREEN_WORKERS = 8`, structured output against
  `VERDICT_SCHEMA`.
- **Categories** `grading`, `course_structure`, `assignments`, `quizzes`,
  `final_exam`. A document matching none is dropped.
- **Output** `relevant` (tri-state), `categories[]`, `reason`, `evidence` --- a
  verbatim quote --- plus `decided_by` (`model` / `format-rule` / `unreadable` /
  `skipped` / `error`).

The prompt's instruction that does the most work is the distinction between
material a course is *about* and material about how it is *run*: lecture slides
explaining gradient descent are `False`; an untitled screenshot showing a
week-by-week table with point values is `True`. It also says to judge content
over filename, and to answer `True` when in doubt --- pass 2 filters again, and a
missed grading rule cannot be recovered.

**Early abort.** A screen is hundreds of requests, so a 400 matching
`FATAL_ERROR_MARKERS` (exhausted balance, invalid key, auth or permission error)
sets a `threading.Event` that stops the remaining work. Discovering an empty
balance on request 1 and stopping is the difference between one error and
hundreds.

`estimate()` counts the input tokens a full run would send via
`messages.count_tokens`, without sending it.

Real run: **243 documents → 211 model calls**, 30 decided on format alone, 2
unreadable, **32 relevant**. 1.07 M input / 15 K output tokens in 62 s.

## Pass 2 --- extraction

One call per course. Input: the step-1 record, then every document pass 1 kept.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  A["course record<br/><i>from SQLite</i>"] --> C["one message"]
  B["relevant documents<br/><i>re-read from corpus</i>"] --> C
  C --> D["claude-sonnet-5-5<br/>effort high · 3 workers<br/>json_schema output"]
  D --> E["proposal"]
  E --> F["credits"]
  E --> G["grading[]"]
  E --> H["mandatory_onsite[]"]
  E --> I["new_activities[]"]
  E --> J["enrichments[]"]
  E --> K["notes"]
  F & G & H & I & J --> L["merge_additive()"]
```

The record goes **first** in the message, so the model knows what is already
answered before it reads anything:

> Here is the record built from Moodle's API so far. Every value in it is
> authoritative --- propose a value only where you see null, and never propose a
> different value for a field that has one.

### What a proposal may contain

| Key | Target | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `credits` | `general.credits` | Only if currently `null` |
| `grading[]` | `grading[]` | Name, `weight_percent`, `type`, `description` |
| `mandatory_onsite[]` | `mandatory_onsite[]` | `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `time`, name, description |
| `new_activities[]` | `quizzes`/`assignments`/`workshops`/`lessons` | Assessments described in prose but absent from the record |
| `enrichments[]` | An existing activity, by `cmid` | Only `ENRICHABLE_FIELDS`, only where `null` |
| `notes` | the report | Contradictions and rules that fit no field |

`grading[].type` is a closed enum: `exam`, `assignment`, `quiz`, `project`,
`presentation`, `participation`, `other`.

**Every entry carries provenance** --- `source` (the document path as given in
its header), `confidence` (`high`/`medium`/`low`), and `quote`, a verbatim
excerpt. The prompt is blunt about it: *a proposal you cannot quote for does not
belong in the answer*. Provenance is what makes a weight checkable without
re-reading the PDF, and the frontend surfaces anything below `high` as a
"check this" badge.

### Budget and ordering

`EXTRACT_MAX_INPUT_CHARS = 600_000` per course. When documents exceed it, the
order decides what survives:

```python
found.sort(key=lambda d: (d.origin != "text", d.chars))
```

Prose before files, smallest first --- so a short page stating the rules is never
what the budget cuts. Anything dropped is reported in `documents_skipped` with
its reason, not silently lost.

### Request shape

- `max_tokens = 32_000`, `effort = "high"`, `format = json_schema`.
- **Streamed**, because `max_tokens` that high risks an HTTP timeout on a
  non-streaming request.
- The system prompt is marked `cache_control: ephemeral`. It is the only stable
  prefix --- the documents that follow differ per course.
- Server-side fallbacks are attempted (`betas=[…]`, `fallbacks="default"`) so a
  declined request is answered by another model in the same call; a 400 naming
  the parameter downgrades to a plain call for the rest of the run.
- `stop_reason == "refusal"` and `== "max_tokens"` are raised as distinct errors
  --- a truncated answer must not be parsed as a complete one.

## The merge

`merge_additive()` is pure: document + proposal → new document + report. The
input is never mutated, and every proposal appears in the report exactly once,
applied or rejected with a reason.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["proposal entry"] --> B{"confidence ≥<br/>min_confidence?"}
  B -->|no| R["rejected"]
  B -->|yes| C{"target field<br/>currently null?"}
  C -->|"no — API set it"| R2["rejected<br/><b>conflict: true</b>"]
  C -->|yes| D{"coerces to<br/>expected type?"}
  D -->|no| R3["rejected"]
  D -->|yes| E["applied"]
```

Five arms, one per target:

| Arm | Identity / gate |
|---|---|
| `_merge_credits` | `general.credits is None` |
| `_merge_list` (grading) | normalised `name` |
| `_merge_list` (onsite) | `(date, normalised name)` |
| `_merge_new_activities` | name not already in that array |
| `_merge_enrichments` | `cmid` exists **and** field is enrichable **and** value is `None` |

Guarantees, enforced in code rather than in the prompt:

- A field holding a value is never written. The attempt is recorded with both
  values and flagged `conflict: true` --- a document disagreeing with the API is
  a finding worth surfacing, not something to resolve silently.
- New entries are **appended**, never substituted, and carry
  `origin: "extracted"` with no `cmid`. Consumers can always tell which rows the
  API asserted.
- Enriched fields record their own provenance under `extracted_fields`, so
  per-field origin survives on an otherwise API-sourced activity.
- Nothing is removed. There is no code path that deletes.
- `_coerce` returns `None` to reject a badly typed value: a wrong-typed field is
  worse than a missing one, since consumers rely on the stored format without
  re-parsing.

A second run proposes the same additions and the merge rejects them all as
already present --- the pass is idempotent.

Real run: **31 additions applied, 0 rejected, 0 conflicts** across 5 courses,
105 K input / 9.6 K output tokens in 37 s.

## Configuration

Everything tunable is in `src/config.py`:

| Setting | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `SCREEN_MODEL` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | Pass 1 |
| `EXTRACT_MODEL` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Pass 2 |
| `SCREEN_WORKERS` / `EXTRACT_WORKERS` | 8 / 3 | Concurrency |
| `EXTRACT_EFFORT` | `high` | Reasoning budget |
| `EXTRACT_MIN_CONFIDENCE` | `low` | Below this: reported, not merged |
| `MAX_TEXT_CHARS` | 60 000 | Per-document text cap (truncation recorded) |
| `EXTRACT_MAX_INPUT_CHARS` | 600 000 | Per-course input budget |
| `SCREEN_MAX_TOKENS` / `EXTRACT_MAX_TOKENS` | 1 024 / 32 000 | Output caps |

The API key resolves in order: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment, then
`.env` (gitignored), then the OS keyring under `anthropic-api-key`.
`resolve_api_key()` returning `None` is not a failure --- it hands resolution back
to the SDK's own chain.

## Known limits

- **No link between a grading component and the activities that satisfy it.**
  `grading[]` and `assignments[]` are parallel lists with nothing joining them.
  A component says "Labs, 30%" and the course has four lab hand-ins, but nothing
  records that those four *are* the Labs component. Any UI showing progress
  toward a grade needs this join.
- **Per-item weights are not modelled.** "4 labs, 5% each" survives only as
  `description` prose.
- **No pass criteria field.** "Weighted grade ≥ 4.0 and the exam ≥ 3.5" has
  nowhere to go in `PROPOSAL_SCHEMA`; it lands in a `grading[].description` or
  in `notes`.
- **Workshops and lessons have no user state.** `is_outstanding`,
  `is_graded_already` and `grade_achieved` are hardcoded `None` in
  `document.py`, so those activities cannot be placed in an open / submitted /
  graded bucket.
